alignment.note: Greek and Latin open with the connective Καὶ / Et; the Peshitta lacks an initial conjunction here, instead fronting the finite verb ܘܫܐܠܘܗܝ which carries its own prefixed waw. The coordinating particle is thus absorbed into the verb form in the Syriac.

Greek uses the accusative of motion εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν ('into the house') and Latin the ablative of place in domo; the Peshitta ܒܒܝܬܐ employs the prefixed preposition beth ('in the house'), agreeing with the Latin static locative rather than the Greek directional sense.

Greek articulates the subject (οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ) with article and separate genitive pronoun, matched by Latin discipuli ejus; the Peshitta condenses 'his disciples' into the single inflected form ܬܠܡܝܕܘܗܝ bearing a possessive suffix, a typical Syriac economy.

Greek περὶ τοῦ τούτου and Latin de eodem ('about the same matter') diverge subtly: the Vulgate's eodem ('the same') implies a previously discussed topic, whereas Greek τούτου and Syriac ܗܕܐ both read simply 'this.' The Latin reflects an interpretive nuance carrying continuity from the preceding pericope.

Greek ἐπηρώτων αὐτόν and Latin interrogaverunt eum render verb plus separate accusative object pronoun; the Peshitta fuses both into the single form ܘܫܐܠܘܗܝ, the verb sh-a-l ('to ask') with an enclitic third-person object suffix, again exhibiting Syriac morphological compression.
